name: Inuyama
tagline: One of Japan's twelve original castles.
intro_en: Inuyama sits on the Kiso River on Aichi's northern edge, crowned by a castle that is one of only twelve in Japan whose main keep has survived intact since the feudal era — and one of just five designated a National Treasure. Climb the steep wooden stairs to the top floor for a sweeping view over the river. Below the castle, the old town's streets are lined with wooden merchant houses, small sake breweries and snack stalls that make for an easy half-day stroll.
In the warmer months the river becomes the stage for ukai, the centuries-old practice of cormorant fishing by firelight, watched from traditional boats.
getting_there_en: Inuyama is on the Meitetsu Inuyama Line from Meitetsu Nagoya Station; the castle and old town are a short walk from Inuyama Station or Inuyama-yuen Station.
